title: 2016 Kumamoto earthquakes
summary: A series of strong shallow earthquakes struck Kumamoto Prefecture in central Kyushu, Japan, in April 2016. A magnitude 6.5 foreshock was followed about 28 hours later by a magnitude 7.3 main shock. They caused 273 deaths, 2809 injuries, 194,888 damaged buildings and evacuations of hospitals, reducing healthcare functionality.

as_recorded.value: The foreshock took place on 14 April 2016 at 9:26PM

importance.justification: Destructive regional earthquake sequence with hundreds of casualties and wide study, but not world-historical.

audience_note: Mentions deaths and injuries from a natural disaster.

sources.title: Post-earthquake hospital functionality evaluation: The case of Kumamoto Earthquake 2016 - Nebil Achour, Masakatsu Miyajima, 2020

reviewer_note: Magnitudes differ by agency: JMA gives 7.3 for the main shock while the ISC lists Mw(GCMT) = 7.0. The ISC origin time of 2016-04-15 16:25:06 appears to be UTC, matching the Japan local time of 16 April 01:25. Casualty figures come from a single hospital-focused paper, and its 'over 3000 casualties' differs from 273 deaths plus 2809 injuries only by rounding. (Drafted by the Wikipedia pipeline from isc.ac.uk, journals.sagepub.com; quotes machine-checked.)
